content: No, that is not correct. In Switzerland, a federal popular initiative is a mechanism that allows citizens to propose amendments to the Swiss Constitution. It does not allow for the proposal of new federal laws. The power to propose new federal laws lies with the Federal Council (the executive branch of the Swiss government) and the Federal Assembly (the legislative branch). The cantons, on the other hand, have more autonomy and can propose new laws or amendments to existing ones through their own legislative processes.
